gappers.catalyst: Neocloud dip-buying on the Jensen Huang reinstatement; no company-specific news.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No NBIS-specific news. The driver is entirely external: NVIDIA's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as President/CEO/director before Monday's open, 11 days after his Nov 12 resignation, and Trump publicly backed the decision. NVDA is +32.7%. Nebius is an AI-infrastructure 'neocloud' renting GPU clusters; it fell 16.1% on Nov 20 to $81.31 as the AI-capex complex de-rated. Its own Q3 (Nov 12) beat on revenue but guided ~$40B of 2027 capex far above consensus, and that guidance, the ~193x P/E and the reported construction delays are all unchanged over the weekend.
gappers.why: Sponsor-risk reversal, not fundamentals. Neocloud equity is a levered call on Nvidia's willingness to keep supplying and financing GPU capacity; Huang's exit repriced that counterparty risk and his return un-prices it. Nothing about Nebius's own economics changed.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day headline spike already mean-reverting. NBIS opened AT its session high of $110.01 and has given back 9.5% to $99.58 in the first 55 minutes - the largest fade on the list and the clearest evidence the gap is being sold rather than accumulated. It is also below the $105.15 the 09:09 ET run marked it at. Session volume 18.9M is heavy but it is the whole complex, not this name: CRWV +22.2% on the identical driver, with BE, AMKR, ORCL and the quantum names all moving together. No idiosyncratic signal; sector read-through is total.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A board reversing its own stated position of six days earlier under public political pressure, with a committee still investigating reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, is headline-driven and reversible - not a structural reset.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing (0/6 positions, 0/3 weekly trades), so the binding constraint is R:R, not the caps. The mandated 10% trail sits at $89.62, inside Friday's $80.68-$93.84 range, so ordinary gap-fill noise stops it out; 2:1 off a 10% risk leg needs +20% to ~$119.50 after the stock has already run 22% and started fading. A stop placed outside Friday's range implies ~22% risk, over twice the 1.0%-of-equity ATR allowance. Also consumes the single AI-infra slot CRWV competes for - correlation far above the 0.75 gate makes the pair one trade, not two.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - fails 2:1 R:R at any sane stop; chasing a reversible headline that is already fading intraday.

gappers.catalyst: Same Huang-reinstatement neocloud driver; credit-spread relief on a heavily levered balance sheet.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Largest listed neocloud, TTM revenue $9.89B (+129.6%) against a reported $66.2B debt load. It fell toward its $40 IPO price last week as that leverage drew scrutiny, closing Nov 20 at $39.51. Supportive items all predate today: Huang's foundation pledged $350M to rent CoreWeave compute, co-founder Brian Venturo bought $30M face value of its bonds, and Citizens JMP reiterated Buy at $180. Nothing new landed today beyond the NVDA headline; a Form 144 (McVeety) was filed Nov 22 and CRWV appeared on Nov 22 after-hours movers lists.
gappers.why: Leverage plus sponsor risk. $66.2B of debt against negative free cash flow makes the equity a levered bet on continued AI capex and cheap financing; Huang's departure widened its implied credit spread and his return narrows it. The analyst note and insider bond buying confirm an existing bull case rather than adding information.
gappers.impact: Credit-driven relief bounce, not a trend change, and already fading - opened $50.80, peaked $51.89, now $48.28 (-7.0% off the high). Still only ~$8 above its IPO price, and the $66.2B refinancing overhang that caused the selloff is untouched. Session volume 34.3M is the heaviest on the list, which cuts both ways: real participation, but into a fade. Read-through identical to NBIS, so holding both adds no diversification. The $350M compute pledge and the insider bond buy are mildly supportive and CRWV-specific, which marginally distinguishes it.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Same reversible CEO headline; the refinancing overhang is unchanged and is what will set the medium-term path.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Competes directly with NBIS for one AI-infra slot - the correlation gate blocks both, so taking either forfeits the other. This is the one name on the list whose 10% trail ($43.45) clears Friday's high ($43.21), so it is the only top-5 setup where the mandated stop is not pure noise-width; but 2:1 then needs +20% to ~$58 on a name that has already run 22% today and is 7% off its high, and the $40 IPO shelf sits just under the stop. Worth noting the scan defect too: on the delayed feed this read +18.94% and the 09:09 premarket run showed the same feed understating it by 2-4x.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - least-bad R:R on the list and the only stop that clears Friday's range, but still requires +20% follow-through from a fading gap on an unresolved leverage story.

gappers.catalyst: BMO upgrade to Outperform, $230 target (Nov 19), finally working now that the AI-power complex is bid.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Bloom Energy builds solid-oxide fuel-cell systems sited directly at customer facilities, and has become the preferred trade on off-grid power for AI data centres. BMO upgraded it to Outperform with a $230 target on Nov 19; the stock gapped up on the news and immediately gave it all back as the Dow fell 1,101 points, then dropped a further 8.5-13% on Nov 20 in the AI selloff (Investor's Business Daily notes another house cut its target to $230). It had fallen ~21.6% over the trailing month into today. Google is a publicly reported customer for its fuel cells, while the bear case is cash burn. It was also named to TIME's America's Top Manufacturers of 2027 list on Nov 18.
gappers.why: An oversold second-derivative AI play with a standing upgrade that the tape would not let work. Data-centre power demand is the bull mechanism and an AI-capex slowdown was explicitly flagged as the key risk; when the Huang headline removed that risk for a session, the upgrade re-priced in one move. ORCL (+12.8%) moving alongside is the same trade - a reported Oracle project is part of Bloom's data-centre pipeline.
gappers.impact: The most sustainable-looking move in the top five on mechanism, and the shallowest fade (-3.9% off a $177.01 high), but the volume argues caution: 6.4M shares is the lightest of the top three by a wide margin, so a +19% move is not volume-confirmed. Unlike ranks 1, 4 and 5 this one has a real documented analyst catalyst, but it is four days stale and was already twice rejected by the market. Sector read-through runs to the whole fuel-cell/AI-power group (FuelCell, Plug both fell with it on Nov 20) plus BW at rank 8 on the same data-centre-power theme.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The catalyst is an analyst upgrade, not a company event - no contract, guidance change or filing - and the cash-burn objection is untouched; a re-rating that depends on AI-capex sentiment holding is not structural. Technology/Industrials is a favoured sector-rotation phase, which is the one argument for the other side.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing, and it is the only top-5 name whose catalyst would satisfy the Entry Checklist's catalyst line on its own terms. But R:R fails: a 10% trail at $153.03 sits inside Friday's $140.73-$162.65 range, so the stop is noise-width, and 2:1 needs +20% to ~$204 - beyond the $230 street target's implied path in a matter of days. Taking it would spend one of three weekly trades on a four-day-old upgrade already bought twice, and it stacks with BW (rank 8) on the identical AI-power theme, so entering both would breach the correlation gate.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - best mechanism on the list and a genuine catalyst, but the mandated 10% stop lands mid-range and 2:1 needs another +20% on unconfirmed volume.

gappers.catalyst: No company news; quantum complex rebounding with the broad tech tape.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No D-Wave-specific news found for today or the weekend. The stock fell 10.8% on Nov 20 to $6.52 on 20.9M shares against a 30-day average of 14.6M - a heavy-volume capitulation day - as part of the broad technology selloff. Street consensus target is $30.00 against a ~$6.51 price, which should be read as stale rather than as a forecast. The whole quantum group is moving as one: RGTI sits at rank 6 on the same non-catalyst, and QTUM (the ETF) is +9.1%.
gappers.why: High-beta small-cap mechanically retracing an oversold low. With no company news the move is fully explained by the index gap plus speculative risk appetite returning to the longest-duration, least-profitable corner of tech - exactly the cohort that falls hardest and bounces hardest without any change in the business.
gappers.impact: Reads as a one-day beta spike likely to mean-revert. Session volume 5.1M is well below Friday's 20.9M capitulation turnover, so the bounce is being made on materially less conviction than the selloff - the clearest volume tell on the list. Already -4.8% off its $7.925 high. Even after +15.7% it has not recovered Friday's loss plus the prior week's. Read-through is the entire quantum complex (RGTI, QTUM, IonQ), confirming zero idiosyncratic signal.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: No catalyst at all, so there is nothing structural to carry; the strategy's own Entry Checklist says to pass when the catalyst line is empty.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing but would spend one of three weekly trades on the thinnest thesis in the top five, and it is strictly dominated by BE (rank 3), which at least has a documented catalyst. R:R fails outright: a 10% trail at $6.79 sits inside Friday's $6.46-$7.28 range and barely above Friday's close, so a routine gap-fill stops it out, while 2:1 needs +20% to ~$9.05. Entering alongside RGTI would breach the correlation gate - the two are one quantum trade.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - no catalyst, fails the Entry Checklist outright, and the bounce volume is a quarter of the selloff volume.

gappers.catalyst: Ethereum-treasury NAV wrapper tracking risk-on; routine holdings update put total assets at $11.1B as of Nov 22.
gappers.catalyst_detail: BitMine Immersion is an Ethereum treasury vehicle - an ~$8.1B market cap wrapped around roughly 6.08M ETH (~4.97% of supply as of Nov 15). The only fresh disclosure is a routine weekend holdings update putting total crypto, cash and 'moonshots' at $11.1B as of Nov 22 15:00 ET, which confirms holdings rather than changing them. No corporate catalyst. It fell 13.9% on Nov 20 to $12.98. B. Riley cut its target to $27 from $34 while keeping Buy; shares are down ~52% over twelve months.
gappers.why: Pure risk-asset beta through a leveraged NAV wrapper. The equity trades at a premium or discount to its ETH stack, so a risk-on reversal moves the stock more than the coin moves. Notably, at an ~$8.1B cap against $11.1B of stated assets the stock is marked below its own stated NAV, which is the only genuinely interesting feature here - and it is a valuation observation, not a catalyst.
gappers.impact: Likely to mean-revert with crypto, and already -3.9% off its $15.60 high. This is the one name in the top five whose driver is NOT the Huang headline, which makes it the only real diversifier on the list - worth recording for correlation purposes even though it fails on its own merits. Sustainability depends entirely on ETH, which this scan did not price, so the read is explicitly low-confidence.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: A holdings-snapshot press release is not structural, and crypto-proxy equities have no thesis independent of the coin; no phase in the TRADING-STRATEGY.md sector-rotation table favours an ETH treasury wrapper.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Displaces nothing, but would spend a trade slot on undiversifiable crypto beta as the account's very first position while the mandate is to beat the S&P 500. The NAV discount gives the stop more logic than the others have, yet a 10% trail at $13.50 still sits inside Friday's $12.88-$15.17 range, and 2:1 needs +20% to ~$18 - achievable only on a large ETH move this scan has no read on.
gappers.verdict: NO ENTRY - no corporate catalyst, undiversifiable single-factor crypto beta, 2:1 R:R unmet.
